Resolve the key pair with `resolvePublicSupabaseEnv({ url: process.env.NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL, publishableKey: process.env.NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_PUBLISHABLE_KEY, anonKey: process.env.NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_ANON_KEY }, { url: 'NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL', key: 'NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_PUBLISHABLE_KEY' })` from `@church/supabase-client` instead of re-implementing the `?? legacy` logic; `maxUploadMb = readMaxUploadMb(process.env.NEXT_PUBLIC_MAX_UPLOAD_MB)` from `@church/domain` (default 50 — founder decision 10); `appUrl` from `NEXT_PUBLIC_APP_URL` with a trailing slash trimmed. `serverEnv()` (imports `server-only`) adds the service pair through `resolveServiceSupabaseEnv({ url, secretKey: process.env.SUPABASE_SECRET_KEY, serviceRoleKey: process.env.SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY })`, plus `SHARE_LINK_COOKIE_SECRET`, `CRON_SECRET`, and the optional `STRIPE_SECRET_KEY`, `STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET`, `STRIPE_PRICE_ID`, `RESEND_API_KEY`, `RESEND_FROM` as `string | undefined`. Missing required values throw an error naming the variable and `docs/ENV.md`. Export `supabaseHost()` (hostname of the Supabase URL) for the CSP.
3. **Supabase clients** (`src/lib/supabase/`), all typed with `Database` from `@church/db/types` and `DbClient`/`ServiceDbClient` from `@church/db`: `server.ts` — `createServerSupabase(): Promise<DbClient>` using `createServerClient<Database>` from `@supabase/ssr` with `await cookies()` (async in Next 16), `getAll`/`setAll`, and `setAll` wrapped in try/catch so Server Components that cannot set cookies do not crash (DESIGN §5). `client.ts` — `createBrowserSupabase(): DbClient` = `getWebBrowserClient({ url, key })` imported from `@church/supabase-client/web` (NOT the package root) with `publicEnv()`. `service.ts` — imports `server-only`; `createServiceSupabase(): ServiceDbClient` = `brandServiceClient(createClient<Database>(url, key, { auth: { persistSession: false, autoRefreshToken: false } }))` with `{ url, key }` from `serverEnv()`'s service pair; a plain unbranded client will not typecheck against `srvAttachUser(svc, …)` in 2.2b or the 2.3/3.4/3.6 helpers, so the brand is mandatory. File-top comment: "service role — only Stripe, push, share resolve, cron and direct user creation may import this (DESIGN §9)". `src/lib/supabase/errors.ts`: `export type ActionError = { key: DomainErrorKey; message: string; field?: string }` and `toActionError(err: unknown): ActionError` — a THIN adapter: `const d = err instanceof DomainError ? err : toDomainError(err); return { key: d.key, message: DOMAIN_ERROR_MESSAGES[d.key] ?? d.message }`. Never match strings in the app: all table/RPC access goes through the `@church/db` wrappers, which already return `DomainError`s (`toDomainError` maps message keys first, then SQLSTATE `42501` → `permission_denied`, `23505` → `duplicate`, `23514`/`22023` → `invalid_payload`). Log the raw error server-side only.
4. **`apps/web/proxy.ts`** (Next 16 middleware file name): create a `createServerClient` with request/response cookie plumbing, call `supabase.auth.getClaims()` (fall back to `getUser()` if the SDK version lacks it) to refresh the session cookie, and redirect unauthenticated requests on protected paths to `/login?next=<encoded original path+query>`. Put the predicates in `src/lib/auth/paths.ts`: `isProtectedPath(p) = p === '/admin' || p.startsWith('/admin/') || p === '/o' || p.startsWith('/o/')` (so `/other` and `/organ` are NOT protected) and `isExcludedFromProxy(pathname)`, both unit-tested.

The CSP body: `default-src 'self'; script-src 'self' 'unsafe-inline'` (Next inline runtime; a nonce-based CSP is a later hardening item — note it in HANDOFF); `style-src 'self' 'unsafe-inline'; img-src 'self' data: blob: https://<supabase host>; media-src 'self' blob: https://<supabase host>; connect-src 'self' https://<supabase host> wss://<supabase host>; frame-src https://www.youtube-nocookie.com https://drive.google.com; font-src 'self' data:; object-src 'none'; base-uri 'self'; form-action 'self'; frame-ancestors <variant>`. ## Constraints
- Versions: Next 16.3.4, React 19.2.3 exact (catalog), `@supabase/ssr` 0.12.5, supabase-js 2.112, Zod 4.5, Tailwind 4.3, shadcn CLI 4.19.1, TypeScript ~5.9 (never 7), ESLint 9 (never 10), Vitest 4.1. Never bump a major. Do not add `expo-*` or `react-native-*` anything. No `.npmrc`.
- Next 16 specifics: the middleware file is `proxy.ts`, `cookies()`/`headers()`/`params`/`searchParams` are async, Server Components cannot set cookies (hence the try/catch in `setAll`). Do not create a `middleware.ts`.
- Reuse, never re-implement, the shared packages: env fallbacks come from `resolvePublicSupabaseEnv`/`resolveServiceSupabaseEnv`, the upload cap from `readMaxUploadMb`, error mapping from `toDomainError`/`DOMAIN_ERROR_MESSAGES`, the scheme from `APP_SCHEME`, the context schema from `myContextSchema`, cache constants from `@church/db/keys`. If a name is missing, add it in the owning package and record it.
- The browser and Server Components use the publishable key only; `service.ts` is created but imported by nothing in this step (standing order: web never holds elevated keys in the client; privileged work runs only in Route Handlers / Server Actions against `srv_*` RPCs). Never expose `SUPABASE_SECRET_KEY` under a `NEXT_PUBLIC_` name.
- Do not build `/login`, `/signup`, `/auth/*`, `/invite/*`, `/admin/*`, `/o/*`, `/s/*`, `/embed/*`, `/api/*` or any Stripe/push/share code (2.1b and later). Do not touch `supabase/`, `packages/*` except the additive exports named above, or `apps/web/vercel.json`.
- Never run `supabase db push` or `db reset`. No secrets or real email addresses in any file; `.env.local` stays untracked (already gitignored as `.env*`).
- No model identifiers in commits or files.

steps.prompt:
You are working in the ChurchAppCLD repository. CLAUDE.md loads `new_session_instructions.md` and `HANDOFF.md` automatically — follow the session-start checklist (new-session.sh, prompt_history.txt). Work on `main` unless I have named another branch in this session. This is step 2.1b "Web auth flow, invite page and admin/org shells" of `docs/TODO.md`; read that step's 'Done when' list first. Read `docs/PLAN.md` §7–§8 and `docs/DESIGN.md` §5 (Supabase Auth — password + 6-digit OTP, the `{{ .Token }}` template requirement, PKCE callback, "Getting accounts" path 1 and the invitation link, super admin bootstrap order), §8 (Invitations email row) and §9 (route groups `(auth)`, `(super)`, `(org)`) before writing code. Build ONLY this step; do not start the next one (2.2a builds the super admin pages).

## Goal
When you finish, a person can sign in and out of Anacast on the web and accept an invitation: `/login` offers a Password tab and an Email-code tab (6-digit OTP with the link fallback that works before the founder edits the Magic Link template in step 2.4), `/signup` creates an account (the bootstrap path of DESIGN §5: sign up → run the `super_admins` INSERT → `/admin`), `/auth/callback` handles PKCE codes, token hashes and Supabase's error redirects, `/auth/reset` requests and completes a password reset, and `/invite/[token]` explains the invitation, accepts it through the `accept_invitation` RPC only on POST, and shows an "Open in app" button built with `inviteDeepLink(token)`. Behind the guards of step 2.1a a signed-in super admin sees the `/admin` shell (sidebar Churches / Fellowships / Super admins; its pages arrive in 2.2a/2.2b) and any signed-in user sees the `/o` landing that lists their active churches (step 3.1 replaces it). `pnpm turbo lint typecheck test` and `pnpm --filter web build` are green; the README documents the Supabase Auth URL configuration the founder needs in steps 2.4/2.5.

## Inputs / prior state
- Step 2.1a built `apps/web` (package `web`): `src/lib/env.ts` (`publicEnv()`, `serverEnv()`), `src/lib/supabase/{server,client,service}.ts` (`createServerSupabase()`, `createBrowserSupabase()`, `createServiceSupabase()` — the last is imported by nothing yet and stays that way in this step), `src/lib/supabase/errors.ts` (`toActionError`), `src/lib/actions/result.ts` (`ActionResult`, `ok`, `fail`), the guards `src/lib/auth/{context,require-user,require-super,require-org,require-perm,landing,paths}.ts` (`getAuthContext()`, `requireUser()`, `requireSuperAdmin()`, `getSuperAdminContext()`, `requireOrgMember(slug)` → `OrgContext`, `requirePerm`, `landingFor(ctx)`, `safeNext(raw)`), `apps/web/proxy.ts` (already redirects anonymous `/admin` and `/o` requests to `/login?next=`), `next.config.ts` with the security headers, `app/layout.tsx` + `providers.tsx` + `globals.css`, `src/lib/brand.ts` (`APP_NAME`, re-exported `APP_SCHEME`), shadcn components under `src/components/ui/*`, the Vitest harness (`server-only` alias, `src/test/setup.ts` with `next/headers`, `next/navigation`, `next/cache` mocks — reuse it) and `apps/web/.env.example`. Read `HANDOFF.md` "Deviations from plan" for whether `forbidden()` or the `notFound()` fallback is live.
- Steps 1.6a/1.6b produced `@church/domain`: `schemas/auth.ts` (`emailPasswordSchema` — password ≥ 8, `otpRequestSchema`, `otpVerifySchema` — email + 6-digit `token`, `passwordResetSchema`), `schemas/invitation.ts` (`acceptInvitationSchema { token }`, `acceptInvitationResultSchema { org_id, slug, membership_id, person_id }`, `invitationTokenSchema` — base64url, 43 chars), `urls.ts` (`inviteDeepLink(token)` → `anacast://invite/<token>`, `inviteUrl(appUrl, token)`), `errors.ts` (`DOMAIN_ERROR_MESSAGES` for `invitation_invalid`, `invitation_expired`, `invitation_email_mismatch`, `organization_suspended`, `minor_cannot_have_account`). Step 1.7a produced `@church/db`: `acceptInvitation(db, { token })` (parsed with `acceptInvitationResultSchema`), `myContext(db)`, `queries/memberships.ts` (`getMyProfile`, `setLastOrg`). Read `packages/domain/src/schemas/{auth,invitation}.ts` and `packages/db/src/rpc.ts` for the exact names; add a missing export in the owning package, never in the app, and record it.
- `9999_init.sql` (1.3b): `accept_invitation(token text) returns jsonb` raises `invitation_invalid` (missing/revoked/accepted), `invitation_expired` (past `expires_at`), `invitation_email_mismatch` (the caller's `profiles.email` must equal the invitation email), `organization_suspended` (via `require_writable`), `minor_cannot_have_account`; it merges an existing member's permissions instead of failing and creates a one-person household (`created_via = 'invitation'`) when `person_id` is null. The `invitations` select policy is `users.create`, so the invite page cannot show the church name before acceptance. The `on_auth_user_created` trigger creates `profiles` from `raw_user_meta_data.display_name`.
- No hosted Supabase project exists yet (step 2.4); verify with the build, unit tests with mocked clients and curl against a mock-env server. The first real sign-in happens in 2.5.

## Build
1. **`(auth)` group scaffolding**: `app/(auth)/layout.tsx` (centred card with `APP_NAME`), client forms with RHF + `zodResolver` using the schemas from `@church/domain` `schemas/auth.ts` — do NOT create `src/features/auth/schemas.ts`; Server Actions in `src/features/auth/actions.ts` (`'use server'`, return `ActionResult`, user client only). Read `?error=` codes in `/login` and render messages for `auth` ("Sign-in link invalid — request a new one"), `expired` ("That link has expired — request a new one"), `email_mismatch` ("This invitation was sent to a different email address — sign in with that address").
2. **`/login`** (`app/(auth)/login/page.tsx`, `src/features/auth/LoginForm.tsx`): tabs **Password** (`signInWithPassword`) and **Email code** (`signInWithOtp({email, options: {shouldCreateUser: false, emailRedirectTo: <APP_URL>/auth/callback?next=…}})` then a 6-digit code field calling `verifyOtp({email, token, type: 'email'})`). Until the founder adds `{{ .Token }}` to the Magic Link template (step 2.4) the email carries a link instead of a code — the callback route handles that link, so both paths land the user; say so in a help line under the code field. On success go to `safeNext(searchParams.next) ?? landingFor(ctx)` (`searchParams` is a Promise in Next 16). Links to `/signup` and `/auth/reset`. Show the `?error=` messages from Build 1.
3. **`/signup`**: email + password (`emailPasswordSchema`, min 8) + display name (1–80) → `signUp({email, password, options: {data: {display_name}, emailRedirectTo: <APP_URL>/auth/callback?next=<next|/>}})`; show "check your email" when no session is returned, otherwise redirect. The bootstrap path in DESIGN §5 ("sign up at `/login` → run the `super_admins` INSERT") is served by the `/login` → "Create an account" link.
4. **`app/(auth)/auth/callback/route.ts`** (`dynamic = 'force-dynamic'`): reads `code` (PKCE → `exchangeCodeForSession`) or `token_hash` + `type` (→ `verifyOtp`), then redirects to `safeNext(next) ?? landingFor(...)`. Supabase sends expired or already-used links back here with `error`, `error_code` (`otp_expired`, `access_denied`, …) and `error_description` instead of the success parameters: put `callbackErrorToKey(searchParams): 'expired' | 'auth' | null` in `src/features/auth/callback-error.ts` (`otp_expired` → `expired`; any other `error` → `auth`; no error → `null`) and redirect to `/login?error=<key>`; the same `/login?error=auth` is used when the exchange itself fails.
5. **`/auth/reset`**: two states — request (`resetPasswordForEmail(email, {redirectTo: <APP_URL>/auth/callback?next=/auth/reset})`) and, when a session exists, set a new password (`updateUser({password})`, `passwordResetSchema`) then redirect to the landing.
6. **`/invite/[token]`** (`app/(auth)/invite/[token]/page.tsx`; `params` is a Promise — `await` it; validate the token with `invitationTokenSchema` and render the generic page even when it is malformed — never 500): explains "You have been invited to a church on Anacast. Sign in or create an account with the email address the invitation was sent to." Signed out → buttons "Sign in" (`/login?next=/invite/<token>`) and "Create an account" (`/signup?next=/invite/<token>`). Signed in → a form whose Server Action `acceptInvitation(token)` in `src/features/auth/actions.ts` calls the `@church/db` wrapper `acceptInvitation(db, { token })` with the USER client (never on GET — mail scanners prefetch links), maps `invitation_invalid` / `invitation_expired` / `invitation_email_mismatch` / `organization_suspended` / `minor_cannot_have_account` via `toActionError` (on `invitation_email_mismatch` also offer "Sign out and sign in with the invited address"), and on success calls `setLastOrg(db, userId, org_id)` and redirects to `/o` (the placeholder below; 3.1 upgrades it to `/o/<slug>/dashboard`). Always render an **"Open in app"** button whose `href` is `inviteDeepLink(token)` from `@church/domain` `urls.ts` — do not hard-code the scheme (DESIGN §5 writes `churchapp://`; the scheme is `anacast` per orchestrator decision 5; note the deviation in HANDOFF). The invitation's church name cannot be shown before acceptance (select policy `users.create`); keep the copy generic.
7. **`signOut`** Server Action (`supabase.auth.signOut()` → redirect `/login`) used by both shells.
8. **`(super)` shell**: `app/(super)/admin/layout.tsx` calls `requireSuperAdmin()` and renders `src/features/admin/AdminShell.tsx` (sidebar: Churches `/admin`, Fellowships `/admin/fellowships`, Super admins `/admin/super-admins`; top bar with the signed-in email from `profile` and a Sign out menu). `app/(super)/admin/page.tsx` is a placeholder card "Churches — built in step 2.2a" so the guarded shell can be seen now. Nothing else under `/admin`.
9. **`(org)` placeholder**: `app/(org)/o/page.tsx` — `requireUser()`, then list the user's churches from `orgs` with `membership_status = 'active'` (name, status badge, link to `/o/<slug>/dashboard` — which 404s until step 3.1; label the section "Church admin area arrives in step 3.1") and a "You are not a member of any church yet — ask your church administrator for an invitation" empty state; super admins see a link to `/admin` and, when they hold no membership, the note "Super admins are not church members: use `/admin`, or accept an invitation to a church to open its admin area" (DESIGN §5; proposed step 3.11 lifts this). Step 3.1 replaces this page.
10. **Tests** (reuse the 2.1a harness): `src/features/auth/callback-error.test.ts` (`otp_expired` → `expired`, `access_denied` → `auth`, no params → `null`), `src/features/auth/actions.test.ts` with a mocked user client — `acceptInvitation` never runs on GET (it is a Server Action; assert the page module exports no `GET`), maps `{ code: 'P0001', message: 'invitation_expired' }` to the catalogue message, calls `setLastOrg` on success; `src/features/auth/schemas.test.ts` — a thin import test proving the forms use `@church/domain` (`otpVerifySchema` rejects a 5-digit code, `emailPasswordSchema` rejects a 7-character password); `src/features/auth/invite-link.test.ts` asserting the rendered invite page (`@testing-library/react`, server component rendered via its async function or a small pure `inviteLinks(token)` helper) contains `inviteDeepLink('abc')` and the `/login?next=/invite/abc` link.

## Constraints
- Versions unchanged from 2.1a: Next 16.3.4, React 19.2.3 exact, `@supabase/ssr` 0.12.5, supabase-js 2.112, Zod 4.5, TypeScript ~5.9 (never 7), ESLint 9 (never 10). No new runtime dependency (shadcn components generated into `src/components/ui/*` are fine).

## Goal
When you finish, a signed-in super admin can run the church side of the platform from `/admin`: see every church with its status, billing mode, subscription badge and trial end; create a church at `/admin/churches/new` (one insert into `organizations`; the `app.on_org_created` trigger creates the settings row, the 6 system audience groups and the 4 default calendars; `trial_ends_at` is set to now + 30 days per founder decision 7); open `/admin/churches/[orgId]` with tabs **Details**, **Settings**, **Fellowships** (plus disabled **Admins** and **Billing** tab stubs that 2.2b fills); edit every `organization_settings` field including the new `sermon_share_allow_download`, the church-configurable youth/adult ages and `push_on_bulletin`; and manage fellowships (`/admin/fellowships`, `/admin/fellowships/[id]`) — create with name, slug and description, edit them, add or remove churches, delete when empty. Everything is done with the user-scoped client under the super-admin RLS policies through the `@church/db` query modules and the `@church/domain` schemas of steps 1.6b/1.7a; the service client is not touched. ## Build
1. **Churches list** — replace the placeholder `app/(super)/admin/page.tsx`: server component, `requireSuperAdmin()`, loads `listOrganizations(db)` from `@church/db` `queries/organizations.ts` (already joins settings + latest `billing_subscriptions`), renders `src/features/orgs/ChurchTable.tsx`: columns Name (link to `/admin/churches/[orgId]`), Slug, Status badge (`trial` grey, `active` green, `past_due` amber, `suspended` red, `cancelled` muted), Billing mode (`manual` / `stripe` / `free`), Subscription badge (from `billing_subscriptions.status`, "—" when none), Trial ends (`trial_ends_at` formatted in the org timezone with date-fns + `@date-fns/tz`, using `settings.timezone`; "—" when null; red when in the past and status still `trial`), Created. 2. **Create church** `app/(super)/admin/churches/new/page.tsx` + `src/features/orgs/ChurchForm.tsx` (client, RHF + `zodResolver`): fields Name (validated by `createOrganizationSchema`: 2–120 chars), Slug (auto-derived from the name with `slugify` in `src/features/orgs/slug.ts` — lowercase, `[a-z0-9-]`, no leading/trailing or double hyphen, trimmed to 48; editable; the slug RULE is `slugSchema` from `@church/domain` (3–48) — the app adds ONLY a `.refine` rejecting the reserved words `admin`, `api`, `o`, `s`, `embed`, `login`, `signup`, `auth`, `invite`, `privacy`, `terms` via `RESERVED_SLUGS`), Contact email (optional), Billing mode (`manual` default, `stripe`, `free`; one-line explanation each: manual = the church pays by check and the super admin tracks status by hand; stripe = card subscription via Stripe, wired in step 2.3; free = no billing, never expires), Trial ends (date, default today + 30 days — founder decision 7: "trial 30 days (`trial_ends_at` default now()+30d on church creation)"; hidden and stored as null when billing mode is `free`, in which case status is inserted as `active`).    - When `organizations.status = 'suspended'` (or `cancelled`), disable the Invite and Create-account buttons with the tooltip "This church is suspended — unsuspend it in the Billing tab before adding administrators" (both `create_invitation` and `srv_attach_user` call `require_writable`).
2. **`src/lib/users/create-direct.ts`** — `createUserDirect(input: z.input<typeof createUserDirectSchema>, deps?)` (imports `server-only`; `deps` allows injecting mocked user/service clients in tests; step 3.2 reuses this exact function for church admins):
   1. Authorisation with the USER client only: `getAuthContext()`; allowed when `isSuperAdmin`, or when the actor holds `users.create` in `input.org` (3.2's church-side dialog); `perms` may be non-empty only when the actor is super admin or also holds `users.edit_permissions` (DESIGN §5: "permissions only if the actor holds `users.edit_permissions`"). Otherwise return `{ ok: false, error: { key: 'permission_denied' } }` without touching the service client. Also read the org with the user client and return `organization_suspended` when `status` is `suspended`/`cancelled` — so no auth user is created and rolled back for a church that `require_writable` would reject anyway.
   2. Validate with `createUserDirectSchema` from `@church/domain` (`org`, `email`, `temp_password` ≥ 12, `display_name`, `person_id` xor `new_household`, `perms` ⊆ `PERMISSION_KEYS`).
   3. Service client (`createServiceSupabase()` — the ONLY place in the web app so far that imports it): `auth.admin.createUser({ email, password: temp_password, email_confirm: true, user_metadata: { display_name } })`. Auth errors come from GoTrue, not the database, so they never pass through `toActionError`: map `error.code === 'email_exists'` (or HTTP status 422) inside this file to `{ key: 'email_exists', message: 'An account with this email already exists — use Invite instead; accepting the invitation links the existing account to this church.' }` (DESIGN §4.4: `accept_invitation` merges for existing users). Add `email_exists` to the local `CreateDirectErrorKey` union (it is not a DB catalogue key). Do not call `listUsers` to look people up by email.
   4. Service client → `srvAttachUser(svc, { user_id: user.id, org: input.org, person_id: input.person_id ?? null, display_name: input.display_name, perms: input.perms })` from `@church/db` (result parsed by `attachUserResultSchema` → `{ membership_id, person_id, household_id }`). `srv_attach_user` has no `new_household` parameter: a null `person_id` makes the RPC build the one-person household and person from `display_name`, so the `new_household` first/last names are NOT forwarded — record this gap in HANDOFF "Deviations from plan" for step 3.2 (a `9998_*` migration could add the parameter). On failure delete the just-created auth user (`auth.admin.deleteUser`) so the call is atomic from the admin's point of view, then return the mapped `DomainError` (incl. `organization_suspended`, `minor_cannot_have_account`) via `toActionError`.
   5. Never log the password; return `{ ok: true, data: { userId, membershipId, personId, householdId, email, tempPassword } }`. The `on_auth_user_created` trigger creates the `profiles` row; `srv_attach_user` sets `display_name`.
3. **Billing tab** `app/(super)/admin/churches/[orgId]/billing/page.tsx` + `src/features/orgs/BillingPanel.tsx`, Server Actions in `src/features/orgs/billing-actions.ts` (all `requireSuperAdmin()`, Zod via `orgBillingFormSchema`/`updateOrganizationSchema`, USER client `updateOrganization(db, id, patch)`; the service client is not used here). Every update requests the row back (`.select('id').maybeSingle()` / `unwrapMaybe`) and treats a `null` row as an error (`permission_denied`) — never toast success on zero rows:
   - **Plan card** quoting founder decision 7: "$50 per month per church, flat; one Stripe recurring Price (`STRIPE_PRICE_ID`); trial 30 days; only `suspended` blocks writes; `past_due` shows a banner only." Show `billing_mode` select (`manual` / `stripe` / `free` with the explanations from `src/features/orgs/billing-mode.ts`) → `setBillingMode(orgId, mode)`; switching to `free` clears `trial_ends_at` and sets `status = 'active'` unless currently `suspended`/`cancelled`; switching to `stripe` shows an info line "Status will be mirrored from the Stripe subscription once 2.3 is deployed (`mirror_subscription_status`); manual status changes are overwritten by the next webhook event."
   - **Trial** (visible for `manual`/`stripe`): `trial_ends_at` date editor with "Extend 30 days" quick action → `setTrialEnd(orgId, date | null)`; helper "When the date passes, the cron's `srv_housekeeping()` moves `trial` to `past_due`; nothing is blocked until you suspend."
   - **Status** card with the current `organizations.status` badge, a table of what each status means (`trial`, `active`, `past_due` = banner only, `suspended` = all writes blocked for the church, reads still work; `cancelled` = purged with its storage 30 days later by `srv_housekeeping`), and actions → `setOrgStatus(orgId, status, { confirmSlug? })`: "Mark active" (from `trial`/`past_due`), "Suspend" (confirm dialog listing consequences), "Unsuspend" (→ `active`, or `trial` when `trial_ends_at` is in the future), "Cancel church" (destructive: requires typing the slug; shows "purges on <date>" computed from the same column `srv_housekeeping` uses — expected `updated_at + 30 days` — and that it cannot be undone after purge), "Reactivate" (from `cancelled` → `active`; show the purge date next to it and hide it once that date has passed). Encode the allowed transitions in `src/features/orgs/status-transitions.ts` (`allowedTransitions(status, mode, trialEndsAt, purgeAt, now)`) and unit-test it. Every change is recorded by the `audit_log` trigger — show "Changes are audited" and a link placeholder to `/admin/audit` (step 6.2).
   - **Stripe card**: read-only rows from `getBillingSummary(db, orgId)` (`billing_customers` customer id; `billing_subscriptions` status badge from `subscription_status`, `status_raw`, `price_id`, `current_period_end`, `cancel_at_period_end`) or "No Stripe subscription"; buttons "Start checkout" and "Open customer portal" rendered `disabled` with the tooltip "Stripe is wired in step 2.3" — reserve their targets as `POST /api/billing/checkout` and `POST /api/billing/portal` in a comment so 2.3 only flips them on. Add `stripeConfigured(): boolean` to `src/lib/env.ts` — true only when `STRIPE_SECRET_KEY`, `STRIPE_WEBHOOK_SECRET` and `STRIPE_PRICE_ID` are all set, reading `process.env` directly so it never throws for other missing variables (`serverEnv()` would throw in the mock-env server) — and when it is false render `src/features/orgs/StripeBanner.tsx`: "Stripe is not configured — missing: <names> (`docs/ENV.md`)". 2.3 reuses both.
4. **`/admin/super-admins`** `app/(super)/admin/super-admins/page.tsx` + `src/features/super-admins/SuperAdminList.tsx`: rows from `listSuperAdmins(db)` (`@church/db`: `super_admins` then `profiles` by `user_id in (...)` — two queries, no embed) showing user id, created_at, display name/email when the profile is visible, "(you)" marker; and an instructions card: "Super admins are `super_admins` rows checked in the database (`app.is_super_admin()`), never a JWT claim, and can only be added or removed in the Supabase SQL Editor". Put the two statements in `src/features/super-admins/bootstrap-sql.ts` as exported constants with `<FOUNDER_EMAIL>` placeholders: `SUPER_ADMIN_INSERT_SQL` = the section (11) INSERT copied verbatim (`insert into public.super_admins (user_id) select id from auth.users where email = '<FOUNDER_EMAIL>' on conflict do nothing;`) and `SUPER_ADMIN_DELETE_SQL` composed here (`delete from public.super_admins where user_id = (select id from auth.users where email = '<FOUNDER_EMAIL>');`) — the migration contains no DELETE, so do not look for one and never edit `9999_init.sql`. The app never reads the migration file at runtime; a unit test reads `supabase/migrations/9999_init.sql` and asserts the INSERT constant appears in it. Also render the bootstrap order from DESIGN §5 (deploy → sign up at `/login` → run the INSERT → reload → `/admin`). Never hard-code a real email.
5. **Navigation and polish**: `AdminShell` "Super admins" entry now resolves; the church header (2.2a) gets a small "Admins: N" count and a "past due" / "suspended" hint. Replace the 2.2a placeholders in `admins/page.tsx` and `billing/page.tsx`.
6. **Tests** (Vitest, reuse the 2.1a harness): `src/lib/users/create-direct.test.ts` with mocked user/service clients — (a) actor without `users.create` and not super → `permission_denied`, service client never called; (b) super admin happy path → `createUser` called with `email_confirm: true`, then `srvAttachUser` with `{ user_id, org, person_id: null, display_name, perms: ALL_PERMISSIONS }`; (c) `email_exists` → mapped error, no `srvAttachUser`; (d) `srvAttachUser` failure → `deleteUser` called, error returned; (e) `perms` non-empty with `users.create` only → `permission_denied`; (f) org `suspended` → `organization_suspended` before `createUser` is called; (g) `createUserDirectSchema` rejects `temp_password` of 11 chars and an input with both `person_id` and `new_household`. `src/lib/users/temp-password.test.ts` (length 16, alphabet, two calls differ). `src/features/orgs/status-transitions.test.ts` covering every transition in Build 3 incl. Reactivate hidden after the purge date. `src/features/orgs/admin-actions.test.ts`: `inviteAdmin` passes `{ org, email, person_id: null, perms }` to `createInvitation` and builds the link with `inviteUrl(appUrl, token)`. `src/features/super-admins/bootstrap-sql.test.ts` (INSERT constant is a substring of the migration; both constants contain `<FOUNDER_EMAIL>`). `src/lib/env.test.ts` gains `stripeConfigured()` cases (all three set → true; one missing → false; no throw when `SUPABASE_SECRET_KEY` is absent).

## Constraints
- The service client is imported by exactly one file in the web app after this step: `src/lib/users/create-direct.ts` (DESIGN §9: "the service client only for Stripe/push/share/cron/direct-create"). Billing status, billing mode, trial, invitations, permissions and membership status all go through the USER client / the `@church/db` client-RPC wrappers.
- Authorisation is checked with the user client BEFORE any service call; never trust `org` from the form without `requireSuperAdmin()` (or the `users.create` check inside `createUserDirect`).
- Reuse, never duplicate: `createInvitationSchema`, `createUserDirectSchema`, `setMembershipStatusSchema`, `orgBillingFormSchema`, `inviteUrl` from `@church/domain`; `createInvitation`, `revokeInvitation`, `setMembershipPermissions`, `setMembershipStatus`, `srvAttachUser`, `listMemberships`, `listInvitations`, `listSuperAdmins`, `getBillingSummary`, `updateOrganization` from `@church/db`. No inline `from('org_memberships')`/`from('invitations')`/`from('super_admins')` in the app; no `profiles(` embed anywhere.
- No Stripe SDK, no `/api/billing/*`, no `/api/stripe/webhook`, no `stripe` dependency — that is step 2.3. No Resend. No `/o/*` pages, no full users grid (3.2), no migrations; do not edit `9999_init.sql`.

- `git grep -ln "lib/supabase/service" apps/web` → exactly `apps/web/src/lib/supabase/service.ts` and `apps/web/src/lib/users/create-direct.ts`.
- `git grep -n "srvAttachUser\|srv_attach_user" apps/web` → only `create-direct.ts` (and its test); `git grep -n "profiles(" apps/web packages/db/src` → nothing; `git grep -n "inviteAdminSchema\|randomBytes" apps/web` → nothing.
- `git grep -n "@gmail\|@yahoo\|@outlook" apps/web` → nothing; `git grep -n "stripe" apps/web/package.json` → nothing.

proposed_additional_steps.title: Super admin access to any church's admin area
proposed_additional_steps.goal: A super admin can open `/o/<slug>/*` for any church without being a member, so the founder can trial the whole web app as super admin (his stated objective) and support churches: `requireOrgMember` accepts `is_super_admin` with `membership_status = null` (as `my_context()` already returns every org for super admins) and the org shell shows a 'Viewing as super admin' banner; writes still pass because `app.perm_org_ids()` returns every org for super admins.
proposed_additional_steps.prompt:
You are working in the ChurchAppCLD repository. CLAUDE.md loads `new_session_instructions.md` and `HANDOFF.md` automatically — follow the session-start checklist (new-session.sh, prompt_history.txt). Work on `main` unless I have named another branch in this session. This is step 3.11 "Super admin access to any church's admin area" of `docs/TODO.md`; read that step's 'Done when' list first. Read `docs/DESIGN.md` §5 (super admin), §6 (helpers return every org for super admins) and `apps/web/src/lib/auth/require-org.ts` before writing code. Build ONLY this step.

## Goal
Super admins can open `/o/<slug>/*` for every church, with a persistent banner, without holding a membership.

## Inputs / prior state
`requireOrgMember(slug)` (2.1a, extended by 3.1) 404s when the slug is not an active membership — including for super admins without a membership (DESIGN §5; the 2.1a code comment points here); `my_context()` returns every org for super admins with `membership_status = null`; `app.perm_org_ids()`/`app.member_org_ids()` return every org for super admins so RLS already allows reads and writes.

## Build
1. `require-org.ts`: accept orgs with `membership_status = null` when `isSuperAdmin`; set `ctx.viewingAsSuperAdmin = true`; keep `writable` derived from the org status and `permissions` = all 12 for super admins (mirrors `app.perm_org_ids`); update the 2.1a unit test that currently asserts the 404.
2. `src/features/org/StatusBanner.tsx`: render 'You are viewing <church> as super admin' with a link back to `/admin/churches/<orgId>`.
3. `OrgSwitcher`: list every church for super admins, grouped 'My churches' / 'All churches'.
4. `/o` landing: super admins see all churches.
5. Audit: nothing extra — DB triggers already record `auth.uid()`.
6. Tests: unit test for the guard; Playwright case in `e2e/` when `E2E_*` env exists.

## Constraints
No migrations; no service client; do not weaken `requirePerm` for non-super users.

## Verify
`pnpm turbo lint typecheck test`; `pnpm --filter web build`; manual: super admin without membership opens `/o/<slug>/dashboard` and sees the banner.

## Finish
Update `HANDOFF.md` (State, remove the 'create yourself as first admin' workaround from the founder to-dos), tick 3.11 in `docs/TODO.md`, write `session_log.md`, commit `feat(web): super admins may open any church admin area`, push.

Non-super users still get 404 on churches they are not active members of (unit test).
The org switcher lists every church for super admins and only memberships for everyone else.
